sections.text: Introduction

According to the directives of the Central Chemical Laboratories this practice 
covers the preparation of Metallographic Specimen for failure analysis.

Failure investigation and subsequent analysis should determine the primary cause 
of failure, and, based on the determination, corrective action should be 
initiated that will prevent similar failures.
Information

Stages of an 
 Analysis

Although the sequence is subject to variation depending on the nature of 
 a specific failure, the principal stages that comprise the investigation and 
 analysis of a failure are as follows:
Collection of Background Data

Collecting the available information regarding the manufacturing, processing 
 and service histories of the failed component including
Power station ( capacity & name ).
Unit Type ( cooler- heater- condenser- boiler ).
Types of tabs ( ASTM, DIM, AIPI....).
Sample location and sectch of the unit.
Date of beginning the operation.
Number of shut down and operation time before failure.
Number of previous failure and the type of maintenance.
Analysis of inner and outer media up to 3 months ago.
Flow rate and the operating temperature and pressure.
Fuel type ( heavy- light- gas ).
Additive used.
Excess air %.
Plant observation.

Sample Collection
Selection of samples should be done prior to starting the examination.

The analyst is responsible for ensuring that the samples will be suitable for 
 the intended purpose and that they represent the characteristic of the 
 failure.

It is often necessary to compare failed components with similar components 
 that did not fail to determine whether the failure was brought about by 
 service conditions or was the result of an error in manufacture.

sections.text:
Preliminary Examination of the Failed Part (Visual Examination and Record 
 Keeping)

The preliminary examination is useful evidence in establishing the cause of 
 failure or in determining sequence of events leading to the failure.

The preliminary examination should begin with unaided visual inspection and 
 before any cleaning.
The examine detect the change of color and texture.
Particular attention should be given to the surfaces of fractures and cracks.

All important features, including dimensions should be recorded either in 
 writing or by sketches or photographs.

sections.text: Mechanical Testing

Hardness testing is the simplest of the mechanical tests and is often the most 
 versatile tool available to the failure analyst. Among its many applications 
 hardness testing can be used to:
Assist in evaluating heat treatment.
Provide an approximation of the tensile strength of steel.

Detect softening or hardening caused by overheating, by decarburization, 
 or by carbon or nitrogen pickup.

Hardness testing measure the resistance to plastic deformation of layers of

Macroscopic Examination

It's detailed examination of fracture surface at magnifications ranging from 1 
 to 100 diameter.

The amount of information that can be obtained from examination of a fracture 
 surface at low-power magnification may give an indication of the type of 
 fracture.

The examination may be done with the unaided eye, hand lens or low-power 
 stereoscopic microscope.

sections.text: Selection and Preparation of Metallographic Sections

Selection and preparation of samples for metallographic or microscopic 
 examination and chemical analysis as in Document Metal-001-r0.
Microscopic ( Metallographic ) Examination
Microscopic examination provide information about:
The failure mechanism.
The method of manufacture of the part under investigation.

The heat treatment to which it has been subjected either intentionally during 
 manufacture or during service.

It provides other service effects such as corrosion, oxidation and severe work 
 hardening of surfaces also are revealed the characteristics of any cracks that 
 may be present.

Metallographic specimen for examination by optical microscope must be prepared 
 as in Document Metal-001-r0.

The optical microscope has been designed by combining various lenses to 
 resolve and reveal the line details of the microstructure of samples.

sections.text: Chemical Analysis

In failure investigation, routine analysis ( bulk, local, surface, corrosion 
 product .... etc ) to ensure that the material is the 
 one that was specified is recommended.

Chemical analysis of any deposit, scale or corrosion product, or the medium 
 with which the affected material has been in establishing the primary cause of 
 failure.

Electron microscope can be used to determine element concentration in alloys 
 and scales.

X-Ray diffraction to identify crystalline compounds of any corrosion 
 products.
